column2: Retain Adam, Seth and Enosh in sequence, with a comma continuing the genealogy. The selected list has no explicit begot verb to insert between these names.
Retain Kenan, Mahalalel and Jared in the ongoing list. No ages or explicit father-son clauses are imported from Genesis.
Retain Enoch, Methuselah and Lamech in order. The shared traditional English names are inherited forms, not newly approved transliterations.
Retain Noah closing the opening sequence and the explicit new heading Noah's sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. The heading distinguishes the three sons from the preceding succession.
Retain all eight entries under Japheth, including Elishah between Javan and Tubal. The selected extra name is not deleted to match another genealogy.
Retain Gomer's three sons Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah. The repeated sons heading supplies the relationship without an added wife or birth order.
Retain Javan's Elishah and Tharsis alongside plural Kitians and Rhodians. The people-group forms remain plural, and Rhodians is not changed to a different consonantal name.
Retain Ham's four sons Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan in source order. No modern geographical identification is substituted for a name.
Retain Cush's five entries and Regma's two, including Saba in each list. Repeated Saba is not treated as an accidental duplicate or proof of identical persons.

Retain Cush begot Nimrod and began to be a giant hunter on the earth. Giant and hunter are both present in the selected Greek; neither a generic mighty man nor an added before-the-Lord phrase replaces them.

Retain the selected shorter Shem heading with Elam, Asshur and Arphaxad and its continuation comma. Units 11–16 and 18–23 are absent from this selected sequence and are not reconstructed from another witness.
Retain Sala as a single-name unit continuing the compressed sequence. No additional generation or explicit begetting formula is supplied to explain the transition from verse 17.
Retain Eber, Peleg and Ragau in order. The genealogy's compression is not expanded into narrated relationships beyond what this selected running list states.
Retain Serug, Nahor and Terah, with the comma carrying the list onward. No incidental biography is added.
Retain Abraham closing the sequence. The selected text gives neither Abram nor an explicit this is Abraham identification to restore.
Retain Abraham's sons Isaac and Ishmael in that order. The order is not changed to chronological birth order in anticipation of the next verse's firstborn expression.

Propose generations of Ishmael, the firstborn for generations of Ishmael's firstborn. This reads the genitive firstborn designation with Ishmael as the genealogy's subject, in keeping with the following list ending these are Ishmael's sons, instead of making the list descendants of an unnamed firstborn son. The close draft retains the inherited construal; Nabaioth, Kedar, Nabdeel and Mabsan remain.
column3: Is firstborn appositional to Ishmael here, or does the compressed construction introduce Ishmael's firstborn Nabaioth? The proposal is a contextual syntactic choice, not an apparatus resolution.

column2: Retain Masma, Idouma, Masse, Choddad and Thaiman as the next five entries in Ishmael's list. The selected name forms are not silently standardized to Genesis.

Retain Jettour, Naphes and Kedma and the explicit conclusion these are Ishmael's sons. This heading supports reading verses 29–31 as a twelve-name list while the firstborn syntax remains separately flagged.
Retain Keturah as Abraham's concubine, her six children and Jexan's Saba and Daidan. She bore him clearly preserves the female subject and male recipient; the relationship is not changed to wife.

Retain Midian's five sons Gaipha, Opher, Enoch, Abida and Eldaa and all these as Keturah's sons. The final summary can embrace descendants and is not rewritten to require immediate maternity for each name.
Retain Abraham begot Isaac and Isaac's sons Esau and Jacob. The repeated Isaac links the generations without changing the inherited begot convention.
Retain Esau's five sons Eliphaz, Ragouel, Jeoul, Jeglom and Kore. No maternal grouping is supplied from Genesis.
Retain Eliphaz's named sons and the special from Timna relation for Amalek. The selected genitive Timna is not turned into a sixth male son alongside Amalek.
column3: Does from adequately express Timna's maternal relation without inserting an absent bore clause?

column2: Retain Ragouel's four sons Nacheth, Zare, Some and Moze. The names remain distinct from similarly formed names elsewhere.
Retain Seir's seven sons, distinguishing Deson from Daison. The similar selected spellings are not collapsed into one English name.
Retain four sons of Lotan: Chorri, Aiman, Ailath and Namna. No sister-Timna clause is imported to replace the selected fourth entry.
Retain Sobal's five sons and Sebegon's Aia and Ana as separate groups. Ana here is not silently identified with every earlier occurrence of that name.
Retain plural sons followed by Ana's single Daison, and Deson's four named sons. The grammatical plural heading and Deson/Daison distinction remain even with one listed descendant.
Retain Osar's three sons and Daison's Os and Arran. No additional identity claim is made between this Daison and the preceding similarly named figures.
Retain the short these are their kings introduction, Balak son of Beor and Dennaba. The selected verse has no explicit before a king ruled Israel clause to add.
Retain Balak's death, Jobab son of Zara from Bosorra and succession in his place. The named king is not substituted from a different Genesis spelling.
Retain Jobab's death and Asom from the land of the Thaimans succeeding. The plural people designation is preserved rather than being made a single town name.

Retain Asom's death, Adad son of Barad, the attack on Midian in Moab's plain and city Geththaim. The participial victory description is attached to Adad contextually, while the patronymic remains intact.
Retain Adad's death and Samaa from Masekka taking his place. The regular succession formula is kept rather than shortened selectively.
Retain Samaa's death and Saul from Rooboth beside the river. The river is unnamed in this unit and is not silently identified as the Euphrates.
Retain Saul's death and Balaennon son of Achobor's succession. No genealogical identity is inferred from Achobor elsewhere in Scripture.

Retain Balaennon's full patronymic at death, another Adad son of Barad and city Phogor. The repeated royal name and father from verse 46 are not harmonized to a different successor; no queen or maternal genealogy is imported.
Retain Adad's death, the transition to Edom's chiefs and repeated Chief before Thamana, Gola and Jetheth. The chiefs are not silently presented as a continuation of the royal succession.
Retain Chief Elibamas, Chief Elas and Chief Phinon with each repeated title. The list's patterned diction is source-grounded rather than ornamental repetition.
Retain Chief Kenaz, Chief Teman and Chief Mabsar. Names shared with earlier genealogical entries do not by themselves establish identical individuals.
Retain Chief Megediel and Chief Heram and the concluding Edom's chiefs formula. The final summary closes eleven titled entries without an added territorial allocation.
